cases.sentence: Война разгоралась, и театр ее приближался к ___.
cases.explain: «русским границам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The war was flaming up and nearing the Russian frontier. Everywhere one heard curses on Bonaparte, “the enemy of mankind.” Militiamen and recruits were being enrolled in the villages, and from the seat of war came contradictory news, false as usual and therefore variously interpreted. The life of old Prince Bolkónski, Prince Andréy, and Princess Márya had greatly changed since 1805.

cases.sentence: Всюду слышались проклятия врагу рода человеческого Бонапартию; в деревнях собирались ратники и рекруты, и с театра войны приходили ___, как всегда ложные и потому различно перетолковываемые.
cases.explain: «разноречивые известия» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: В 1806 году ___ был определен одним из восьми главнокомандующих по ополчению, назначенных тогда по всей России.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In 1806 the old prince was made one of the eight commanders in chief then appointed to supervise the enrollment decreed throughout Russia. Despite the weakness of age, which had become particularly noticeable since the time when he thought his son had been killed, he did not think it right to refuse a duty to which he had been appointed by the Emperor himself, and this fresh opportunity for action gave him new energy and strength. He was continually traveling through the three provinces entrusted to him, was pedantic in the fulfillment of his duties, severe to cruel with his subordinates, and went into everything down to the minutest details himself. Princess Márya had ceased taking lessons in mathematics from her father, and when the old prince was at home went to his study with the wet nurse and little Prince Nikoláy (as his grandfather called him). The baby Prince Nikoláy lived with his wet nurse and nurse Sávishna in the late princess’ rooms and Princess Márya spent most of the day in the nursery, taking a mother’s place to her little nephew as best she could. Mademoiselle Bourienne, too, seemed passionately fond of the boy, and Princess Márya often deprived herself to give her friend the pleasure of dandling the little angel—as she called her nephew—and playing with him.

cases.sentence: Княжна Марья перестала уже брать у своего отца ___, и только по утрам, сопутствуемая кормилицей, с маленьким князем Николаем (как звал его дед) входила в кабинет отца, когда он был дома.
cases.explain: «математические уроки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: In 1806 the old prince was made one of the eight commanders in chief then appointed to supervise the enrollment decreed throughout Russia. cases.sentence: У алтаря лысогорской церкви была часовня над могилой ___, и в часовне был поставлен привезенный из Италии мраморный памятник, изображавший ангела, расправившего крылья и готовящегося подняться на небо.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгини» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Near the altar of the church at Bald Hills there was a chapel over the tomb of the little princess, and in this chapel was a marble monument brought from Italy, representing an angel with outspread wings ready to fly upwards. The angel’s upper lip was slightly raised as though about to smile, and once on coming out of the chapel Prince Andréy and Princess Márya admitted to one another that the angel’s face reminded them strangely of the little princess. But what was still stranger, though of this Prince Andréy said nothing to his sister, was that in the expression the sculptor had happened to give the angel’s face, Prince Andréy read the same mild reproach he had read on the face of his dead wife: “Ah, why have you done this to me?”

cases.sentence: Вскоре после возвращения князя Андрея, ___ отделил сына и дал ему Богучарово, большое имение, находившееся в 40 верстах от Лысых Гор.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Soon after Prince Andréy’s return the old prince made over to him a large estate, Boguchárovo, about twenty-five miles from Bald Hills. Partly because of the depressing memories associated with Bald Hills, partly because Prince Andréy did not always feel equal to bearing with his father’s peculiarities, and partly because he needed solitude, Prince Andréy made use of Boguchárovo, began building and spent most of his time there.

cases.sentence: Все сутки эти, не доверяя своему ___ и ожидая того, за которым было послано в город, они предпринимали то то, то другое средство.
cases.explain: «домашнему доктору» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was the second night that neither of them had slept, watching the boy who was in a high fever. These last days, mistrusting their household doctor and expecting another for whom they had sent to town, they had been trying first one remedy and then another. Worn out by sleeplessness and anxiety they threw their burden of sorrow on one another and reproached and disputed with each other.

cases.sentence: — проговорил он сердито, и выслушав ___ от отца и взяв подаваемые конверты и письмо отца, вернулся в детскую.
cases.explain: «словесные приказания» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Devil take them!” he muttered, and after listening to the verbal instructions his father had sent and taking the correspondence and his father’s letter, he returned to the nursery.

cases.sentence: Старый князь, на ___, своим крупным, продолговатым почерком, употребляя кое-где титлы, писал следующее:
cases.explain: «синей бумаге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He still had all the letters in his hand. Opening them mechanically he began reading. The old prince, now and then using abbreviations, wrote in his large elongated hand on blue paper as follows:

cases.explain: «другой конверт» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy sighed and broke the seal of another envelope. It was a closely written letter of two sheets from Bilíbin. He folded it up without reading it and reread his father’s letter, ending with the words: “Gallop off to Kórchevo and carry out instructions!”
